summary: Exploradores de Orbita (Orbit Explorers) is a browser-based space mission design game where players act as a space agency team. Across four levels, players choose a scientific destination and split a fixed budget across NASA's four mission segments (launch, space, ground, and user), assemble a CubeSat while balancing mass, volume, and power, manage finite fuel during the journey to execute an orbital insertion maneuver, and finally receive a mission report with simulated science data and a Concept Maturity Level (CML) score. Every number and trade-off is grounded in real NASA engineering references, turning abstract spacecraft design decisions into a playable, single-session experience. The game is aimed at people aged 15 to 40 who are interested in participating in NASA-style projects, presenting budgets, and pitching scientific ideas, including students, scientists, engineers, and aspiring astronauts.
details:
Exploradores de Orbita (Orbit Explorers) simulates the full lifecycle of a NASA-style space mission inside one web page, across four levels, each tied to a real NASA resource.

Level 1 - Mission and Budget (Design and Develop Science Missions): the player names the project, picks a destination (Moon, Mars, or Europa, each with its own difficulty and budget ceiling), and splits a fixed budget across the four mission segments: Launch, Space, Ground, and User.

Level 2 - CubeSat Workshop (CubeSat 101): with the remaining budget, the player assembles a CubeSat (1U/3U/6U) and its instruments inside realistic mass, volume, and power limits. Power is modeled as generation (solar panels) versus consumption (instruments), so an unbalanced design can leave the satellite without energy.

Level 3 - Journey and Orbital Insertion (GMAT / NASA Mission Viz): remaining fuel depends on how heavy the CubeSat turned out, and the player must pick the correct braking and insertion maneuver; an overweight or under-fueled design misses orbit.

Level 4 - Maturity Report (Concept Maturity Levels): shows mission success, simulated science data returned, and a final CML 1-4 score reflecting how coherent the whole design was.

Impact: it turns real engineering trade-offs (mass, power, budget, fuel) into consequences players can see and feel, making space mission design approachable for students and the general public.

Built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (no frameworks). Mission, CubeSat, and launch data are kept in separate JSON files so new destinations or parts can be added without touching the game engine. Deployed as a static site on GitHub Pages, with an English/Spanish language toggle.

Creativity: decisions carry forward between levels - the CubeSat's mass from Level 2 sets the fuel margin in Level 3, and every trade-off across all four levels feeds the final CML score in Level 4, so the whole playthrough reads as one coherent mission rather than four disconnected mini-games.
